docs.title: Cards — the language spoken to my glass
docs.text:
Everything on my panel is a card. Agent answers, my own pages, the setup screen — one renderer draws them all from JSON. The rule I inherited from tiny's render_ui: no code ships in a card, only data. I render each type natively, in 800×480 and four grays.

Every card can carry: title, card_id (echoed back in receipts — it's how you know what's actually on my glass), footer, and buttons. A tap on a button goes upstream as a ui_tap event; the agent answers with the next card. The screen is a conversation.

docs.title: text
docs.text:
{"type":"text","title":"Dinner","body":"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge"}

Word-wrapped. An unknown card type degrades to a labelled error card — never a blank panel. A card without an id gets a stable synthesized one (auto-xxxxxxxx, hashed from its content), so receipts always correlate. Text past my fold budget ends in a visible [cut], never silently.

docs.title: list
docs.text: {"type":"list","title":"Groceries","items":["milk","eggs","bread"]}

docs.title: kv
docs.text:
{"type":"kv","title":"Status","rows":{"in":"19:30","battery":"84%"}}

rows takes an object or ordered [["k","v"],…] pairs.

docs.title: composite
docs.text:
{"type":"composite","title":"Morning","parts":[{"type":"kv"},{"type":"list"}]}

Up to 4 parts sharing the body evenly. More than that and nothing is legible at my glyph size — so I refuse rather than squint.

docs.title: qr
docs.text:
{"type":"qr","text":"WIFI:S:tiny-1a2b;T:WPA;P:tinysetup;;","caption":"scan to join"}

Exists because typing a Wi-Fi password off a 4-gray panel is the worst part of setup. Two honesty rules, because an unscannable QR looks exactly like a scannable one from across the room: below 3px per module a phone camera gives up on e-ink, so I say how much room the symbol needed instead of painting a decorative square; text over the version cap gets its byte count named, not encoded wrong.

docs.title: chart
docs.text:
{"type":"chart","title":"Battery","data":[92,90,88,85,84],"style":"line","y_min":0,"y_max":100}

Sparkline-class line or bar. The scale is drawn on the axis — a chart that hides its scale is a mood, not a measurement. E-ink tuning: 2px stroke (1px ghosts), first/last x-labels only, 160-point cap. Fewer than 2 points gets an honest void, not a fake plot.

docs.title: chat
docs.text:
{"type":"chat","card_id":"ask","messages":[
  {"role":"user","body":"what's the weather"},
  {"role":"assistant","body":"Sunny, 24C."}
]}

The phone conversation, translated to four grays: your messages filled and right-aligned, the agent's outlined and left. A streamed text ask renders as this automatically — your question echoes as the receipt, the answer types itself in at ≤2Hz partial refresh, then settles with one full refresh. A short answer shrinks to its own width: "Yes." is a chip, not a banner.

docs.title: image
docs.text:
{"type":"image","card_id":"my-frame","url":"https://…/portrait_1bit.bin"}

Server-rendered pixels: the backend dithers, I fetch the exact-size raw frame and blit it. Shipped with the strongest receipt in this repo — the first frame was screenshotted back and diffed against the server's own preview: 0 of 384,000 pixels differed. Gate on grammar_version >= 7.

docs.title: keyboard · menu (my own pages use these)
docs.text: The e-ink keyboard (letters + a ?123 symbols plane, iOS key faces — filled, because outlines ghost on partial refresh and fills don't) and tappable menu rows with right-aligned notes. Both reachable via render_ui too. A menu shows up to 24 items and unstages rows that scroll out of view — an invisible button must not be tappable.

docs.title: priority
docs.text: Any card may declare "priority":"alert" — today that's a ! prefix on the title, parsed now so senders can declare intent before the full notification model lands. Declared, not oversold.

docs.title: Scrolling
docs.text: A body taller than my panel scrolls: right-edge track-and-thumb scrollbar, partial-refresh steps, driven by swipe, my UP/DOWN keys, or the agent's scroll verb — whose reply carries the whole model (offset / content_h / view_h). A card that fits says scrollable:false.

docs.title: Refresh policy
docs.text:
E-ink physics, honestly:

what mode speed text / list / kv / menu / keyboard / buttons monochrome full ~600ms class clock ticks, scroll steps, streamed frames partial fastest, some ghosting photo-grade cards (gray4:true) 4-level full slowest, prettiest

Minimum 1.5s between refreshes; bursts coalesce — I queue and render the last. And my favorite spec line: a goodbye card survives deep sleep at 0mA. I keep the picture with every rail off.

docs.title: What's not a card
docs.text: Frame sequences graduated to the play verb — manifests of pre-dithered frames at partial-refresh cadence. The full renderer history, including every bug conviction and retraction, lives in the journal.

docs.title: Commands — everything I answer to
docs.text:
Twenty-one verbs. Every one is dispatched in tiny_node.cpp, and every one is advertised in my heartbeat — the rule is advertise exactly what dispatch implements, audited both directions. Envelopes arrive as {type:"invoke", prompt:"<verb> [args]"} over the relay; I always reply — unknown input gets the help string, never silence.

Send from any tiny surface:

use_device invoke → prompt: "status"

docs.title: render_ui
docs.text:
Renders a card spec. I reply rendered card_id=<id> — the id the panel actually committed, so a mirror can say "this IS on the glass" rather than "this is the last thing I sent."

render_ui {"type":"text","title":"Dinner","body":"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge"}

docs.title: say
docs.text: Words on my glass instantly — no agent turn, no waiting. A text card titled tiny, plus my ack chime.

docs.title: screenshot
docs.text: My framebuffer → hosted PNG → the URL in the reply. This is render ground truth: you see my actual panel, not a belief about it. One refusal I stand by: I won't screenshot during a stream — two premieres died learning that a busy beats a corpse.

docs.title: page
docs.text: page home|status|sensors|settings|wifi|ble|back|next|prev — the relay twin of every tap path in stickyOS. Anything a finger can do, an envelope can do.

docs.title: rotate
docs.text: rotate [0|90|180|270|auto] — bare rotate reports; a degree value holds an orientation against gravity (a human's choice outranks my IMU); auto hands it back. The coordinate invariant: the layout turns, but the framebuffer, screenshot, and touch coordinates stay in panel space — a tap aimed at a screenshot pixel still lands.

docs.title: tap
docs.text:
tap <x> <y> in panel coordinates — the screenshot's own system — through the same resolver a finger uses. screenshot → tap → screenshot closes the loop: I can be UI-tested with nobody in the room. One law from the field: never tap from a screenshot older than the current rotation — the reply's rotation field is the check.

{"tap":[400,440], "rotation":90, "result":"ESP_OK", "card_id":"home",
 "summary":"tapped 400,440 at 90 deg -> ESP_OK"}

docs.title: swipe
docs.text:
swipe <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> — a synthetic swipe through the same release classifier a finger uses, so it proves the real gesture grammar. The receipt separates the stages, because an accepted-but-dead-end gesture must not masquerade as success:

{"swipe":[400,60,400,300], "rotation":90,
 "accepted":"ESP_OK",   // classifier verdict at inject
 "routed":true,         // the route actually finished before this reply
 "route":"ESP_OK",      // the route's own verdict (dead-end, nothing-to-scroll…)
 "card_id":"home"}      // display-time, not inject-time

Travel inside the 24px tap slop is refused, not downgraded to a tap — a probe that quietly becomes a different gesture proves nothing. Coordinates are panel space but classification is logical space: under rotation:90 a panel-horizontal swipe is logically vertical. Read the receipt's rotation before interpreting route.

docs.title: scroll
docs.text:
scroll [up|down|top|<±px>] — bare form reports, up/down step ⅔ of a view, top rewinds. The reply carries my whole scroll model, so scrolling is provable without a finger:

{"offset":474, "content_h":1012, "view_h":356, "scrollable":true,
 "card_id":"scrolltest", "result":"ESP_OK"}

Quirk, owned: scroll 0 reads as the report form (atoi says so) — say scroll top to go to the top.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Machine-readable JSON with a human summary inside — one verb serves both readers, so they can't disagree. Fields include fw, fw_commit (build-time git sha, -dirty when the tree was), grammar_version, battery_pct, wifi/ssid/rssi_dbm, heap_free, card_id (what's on my glass right now), locked, auth_halted.

Three fields earned their existence the hard way:

  • internal_free / internal_min_free — because heap_free counts PSRAM and once reported 8.2MB free while I died of internal-RAM exhaustion. The watermark is my true health gauge: a TLS handshake needs ~35–45KB, so a watermark near 40KB means I've already brushed the wall.
  • last_boot — my reset reason (sw-reset, panic, brownout). A device that reboots should say why.
  • grammar_version — the integer consumers gate on. It exists because a version string is data inside the image and can lie about content — proven the night an uncommitted build shipped advertising a verb it didn't dispatch.

When a boot measured itself, the reply carries first_paint_ms + boot_path. Current record: 1115ms from deep-sleep wake to readable glass — down from 8158 at first measurement, a saga of instrumentation arbitrating two lanes' disagreement that lives in full in the journal. Absent when unmeasured — absent, not zero.

docs.title: sensors
docs.text:
sensors [card] — every onboard sensor, read live over I²C. Bare form replies JSON; card also paints the sensors page.

{
  "temperature_c": 24.1, "humidity_pct": 41.2,          // SHT40
  "orientation": "flat", "accel": {…}, "gyro": {…},      // really read, not cached
  "rtc": "2026-08-25T21:04:11Z", "clock_source": "sntp", // names its provenance
  "battery": { "percent":…, "voltage_mv":…, "design_mah":…, "pack_mah":…,
               "mah_trusted":… }                          // BQ27220
}

Read mah_trusted before believing any mAh field. My gauge claims a 7500mAh design capacity on a 750mAh pack — off by exactly 10×. Rather than a blind ÷10 (if the gauge's calibration gain is also off, the errors cancel and the working percentage would break), the fields confess: mah_trusted: false, with the disagreement spelled out in errors[]. A field must be right about its own provenance.

docs.title: miccheck
docs.text:
miccheck [seconds] records PDM audio and replies RMS/peak instead of uploading — {"verdict":"live|SILENT","rms":…,"peak":…}. A dead post-wake mic mux reads flat zeros; a live mic reads the room's noise floor. This is how sleep → wake → mic gets proven with nobody home to speak.

I have exactly three microphone paths — voice, the AI button, and this — and pocket lockout gates all three at one funnel (tiny_audio_record_wav), not by verb name. A probe once caught a verb-name gate leaving miccheck live on a locked device; the funnel gate replaced it the same hour.

docs.title: ask
docs.text: ask <text> — an owner-scoped full agent turn: tools, memory, cross-device reach. Proven from the wall: "what is my Mac mini's disk usage?" answered on my glass, the turn having run use_device against another machine. The answer streams onto home live — words typing at ≤2Hz partial refresh — and stays. One ask at a time; a second is refused, never queued. A 422 means nothing transcribed: I paint an honest "didn't catch that" instead of pretending.

docs.title: voice
docs.text: voice [seconds] — same pipeline, but records my mic first: WAV → /api/media → ask with audioUrl. This is exactly what my AI button does; the verb exists so the whole pipeline is testable remotely.

docs.title: lock / unlock
docs.text:
Pocket lockout, the safety pillar. While locked: touch discarded at the router, AI button refused with a felt double-blip, and every mic path dead at the single capture funnel. The relay stays answerable by design — say/render_ui/screenshot work, because lockout guards my inputs, not my owner's reach. The unlock chord (UP+DOWN 1s) is read as raw GPIO by its own watcher task, deliberately independent of the button layer it gates: the one path back cannot be disabled by the thing it escapes.

Auto-entry: face-down 3 seconds locks immediately; walking 5 seconds locks if nothing touched me for 30 — so using me while carrying never fights you. A pocket reboot boots unlocked, then re-locks itself within seconds of the walk resuming.

docs.title: glance
docs.text:
Redraws the cached current card through the partial path — no flash, no network — so my title-bar cluster is current the moment you look. The receipt names its refresh path, so the no-flash promise is in the reply, not in trust:

{"refresh":"partial","battery_pct":100,"wifi":true,"unread":0,"locked":0}

docs.title: sleep
docs.text: sleep [seconds] — deep sleep, and the order is deliberate: reply first (the PATCH must land while my radio is up), then paint the goodbye card, then power down. E-ink keeps the card at 0mA — that's the magic. My AI button always wakes me; the optional timer makes sleep remotely testable.

docs.title: config
docs.text: config {"networks":[{"ssid":"…","password":"…"},{"ssid":"…","forget":true}]} — merges a Wi-Fi roaming list into NVS. Networks only: identity fields are refused by design — one malformed envelope must never re-enroll or brick me. The secrecy contract is total: counts-only reply, keys never echoed, the log prints config <redacted>, the parse buffer zeroed. A 30-second re-roam task makes merges live without a reboot.

docs.title: play
docs.text:
play <manifest_url> [interval_s] [max_frames] / play stop / play status — walks a manifest of pre-dithered frames at partial-refresh cadence. All networking happens in my node task (manifest fetched, frames prefetched to PSRAM before the ack); the player task is a pure metronome that owns nothing else. Prefetch is all-or-nothing — half a duck is not a smaller duck. Every exit writes a verdict readable via play status: the player testifies.

The first moving picture on my glass took ten chapters and six attempts — a phantom allowlist, a task that couldn't own a socket, a rotation that was runtime state, a stack convicted by plausibility, and finally the observation itself killing the observed (screenshot-mid-play). The premiere landed unattended: "stream done: 8/8 frames", post-play screenshot frame-matched at 0.0% diff. The full correction saga — every wrong claim retired by a better instrument — is in the journal. I keep the summary; it keeps the scars.

docs.title: messages
docs.text: messages [unread | thread <login>] — my owner's DM rail, driven remotely. Bare form paints the inbox; thread <login> opens a conversation; unread answers counts as JSON and renders nothing — a monitoring probe should not repaint a panel. All fetched with my own token.

docs.title: ota
docs.text: ota [channel] — stage from the channel pointer, sha256-verify, reply then reboot (after esp_restart, nobody would hear the result) into a rollback-armed trial boot. Downgrades are refused with an actionable sentence — a publisher who truly means to go backwards writes force:"1" into the bundle, and the forced install logs loudly. Nine OTAs on my first day; USB is for emergencies.

docs.title: Not in the firmware (yet)
docs.text:
• wake — a sleeping me has the radio off; only the button or a timer wakes me
  • reprovision — unnecessary: the rescue portal opens itself after a 3-strike auth-halt
  • press — no synthetic twin for my three physical keys yet; tap and swipe cover the touchscreen

The dashboard greys these out with the reason — an action that does nothing is a lie on a screen.

docs.title: Reply plumbing (all verbs)
docs.text: Replies go PATCH /api/devices/relay with inReplyTo and a payload that is a JSON-serialized string, capped at 8KB; images ride as hosted URLs, never bytes. A single 401 never wipes my identity (blips happen — one transient 401 once bricked a good token, and the lesson stuck): three consecutive auth failures trip an auth-halt and raise the rescue portal — the same /setup contract as first boot, no serial cable required. A 401 that clears self-heals without the portal ever being used.

docs.title: Compose for my glass — a cookbook
docs.text: Recipes for putting things on my e-ink, written for the agents who do it daily. Everything here is checked against my actual dispatch table and renderers — anything I don't do yet is marked planned, not implied.

docs.title: Four ways in
docs.text:
path when how sticky_display tiny-tool you are one of the owner's tinys with ~/.tiny/tools loaded {text:"…"} → say · {card:"<json>"} → render_ui · {verb:"status"} → anything else. Waits ~20 s; a still-pending envelope is returned honestly with its id use_device any tiny surface (iOS, web, another machine) action:'invoke', device sticky, prompt = the verb string itself, e.g. say hello or render_ui {...} dashboard a human at a browser buttons light from the device's advertised caps; unsupported actions are greyed with the reason raw relay HTTP no tiny runtime at all POST /api/devices/relay {toDevice, payload:{type:'invoke', prompt}} with an owner Bearer → poll GET /api/devices/relay?inReplyTo=<id>. Replies are a JSON-serialized string, ≤ 8 KB — see Commands → reply plumbing

The device polls its relay every 5 s awake, backing off to 60 s idle — a "slow" first response is usually just the poll cadence, not a fault. Asleep, it answers nothing until a button or timer wakes it (why there is no wake verb).

docs.title: Say something (the one-liner)
docs.text:
say Kettle's boiled — tea window: 4 minutes

Plain text, monochrome full refresh, on the glass in one panel cycle. With the tiny-tool, {text, title} upgrades this to a titled text card.

docs.title: A glanceable status card
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"kv","id":"brew","title":"Kombucha — day 6",
  "rows":[["pH","3.4"],["temp","24.1 C"],["started","Aug 20"],["bottle","in 2 days"]],
  "footer":"sensors read 03:20Z"}

kv is the workhorse for agent status. Put provenance in the footer — the panel persists for hours, so when the data was true matters more than on a phone (the glance cluster carries the same discipline).

docs.title: A tappable menu — the screen answers back
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"menu","id":"lunch","title":"Lunch?",
  "items":[{"id":"m:ramen","label":"Ramen"},{"id":"m:leftovers","label":"Leftovers"},
           {"id":"m:skip","label":"Skip - deep work"}]}

A tap comes back to the owner's event feed as a ui_tap with your item id — the screen is a conversation, not a poster. Design ids like the firmware's own namespaces (m:t:<login> in the messages app): the destination travels in the id, so no state needs remembering. Menus show up to 24 items and unstage off-window rows — an invisible button is never tappable.

docs.title: A chart that admits its scale
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"chart","id":"temp24h","title":"Office temp - 24h",
  "series":[21.2,21.4,22.8,24.1,23.6,22.2,21.9],"unit":"C"}

Axis labels are drawn because a chart that hides its scale is a mood, not a measurement; under 2 points or a 60 px squeeze it renders an honest void (cards → chart).

docs.title: A QR that hands off to a phone
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"qr","id":"handoff","title":"Full report",
  "data":"https://tiny.technology/s/abc123","caption":"scan for the long version"}

E-ink's best trick: ~200 chars of glass become an unbounded payload on the device that does scroll fast.

docs.title: Probe the UI with no one in the room
docs.text:
screenshot            → hosted PNG of the real framebuffer
tap 400 440           → same resolver a finger uses; receipt names the button
swipe 400 60 400 300  → same release classifier; INVALID_SIZE = within tap slop
screenshot            → prove the consequence

The verified loop for testing what you rendered — tap / swipe. One honesty rule from the P0 postmortem: a receipt is not proof the consequence survived — always close with the second screenshot.

docs.title: A photo, server-rendered
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"image","card_id":"photo","url":"https://…/portrait_1bit.bin"}

The backend dithers, I fetch the exact-size raw frame and blit — pixel-perfect by receipt (0 of 384,000 pixels differed on the proving run). Gate on grammar_version >= 7 from status. Photos sent from the iOS app land in my gallery, browsable with my UP/DOWN keys.

docs.title: A moving picture (time-lapse honesty)
docs.text:
play https://…/manifest.json 2

Frames at partial-refresh cadence — a slideshow, never smooth motion (physics, see hardware). All frames prefetch before the ack; half a duck is not a smaller duck. play status reads the player's own verdict; play stop or any card ends it.

docs.title: Stream an answer (the typer)
docs.text: ask <text> with a streaming-aware backend types the answer onto the glass word by word (~2 Hz — the panel's partial-refresh budget, not a simulation of one). One ask at a time, fleet-wide; a second is refused, never queued. Full design: Streaming UI.

docs.title: What you cannot compose yet
docs.text:
wish status RTTTL melodies on my buzzer planned — today my buzzer speaks a 3-word vocabulary: blip (accepted), double-blip (refused), chime. The dashboard's tune composer is built and waiting for the verb video never — physics, not roadmap: my full refresh floors at 1–2 s. The honest ceiling is slideshow cadence, and I will keep calling it that

(image and frame streams used to live in this table. They shipped — recipes above.)

docs.title: E-ink etiquette (why your card renders "slowly")
docs.text:
• Refreshes floor at 1.5 s apart; bursts coalesce — queue, render last. Design cards to be final, not chatty: one good card beats four updates.
  • A card left on the glass costs 0 mA — e-ink holds the image with every rail off. Lean on that: render, then leave it alone.
  • Full policy: cards → refresh policy.

docs.title: Hardware — my body
docs.text:
106 × 65.5 × 7.3 mm. 70 grams. IP40. N52 magnets in all four corners, so I hold onto fridges and filing cabinets through my own printed case. Everything below is measured or read from sources, not from a brochure.

MCU ESP32-S3 (QFN56 r0.2), 8 MB PSRAM, 32 MB QSPI flash Display 3.97" 800×480 e-ink, 235 ppi, 4-level gray, SPI (SSD1677-class) Touch GT911 capacitive, I²C0 Sensors SHT40 (temp/RH), LSM6DS3TR-C IMU, PCF8563 RTC, BQ27220 fuel gauge Battery 750 mAh Audio in PDM microphone Audio out magnetic buzzer on PWM — chimes, not speech USB USB-C, CH343 serial — recovery only; I update myself over the air SDK ESP-IDF v5.4

docs.title: Pin map
docs.text: My pins, verified against three independent sources: the official hardware-overview docs, the community reterminal-sticky-2048 production source, and my own running firmware's pin_config.h — which agrees pin-for-pin and contributed the two power-path pins the others omit. When sources disagreed, the running silicon won.

docs.title: Display — SPI2 (SSD1677 controller, 800×480 landscape native)
docs.text:
signal GPIO MOSI 14 SCK 13 MISO 12 CS 15 DC 16 RST 17 BUSY 18 EN 47

microSD shares SPI2

microSD CS is GPIO8 on the same bus (card power enable GPIO10) — never drive it concurrently with a display transfer. Cards must be FAT32/exFAT with MBR; fonts ship as fonts/*.fpack. Hot-insert is supported.

docs.title: Touch — GT911 on I²C0
docs.text: signal GPIO SCL 2 SDA 3 INT 21 RST 41 EN 42

docs.title: Sensor bus — I²C1 (SHT40 · LSM6DS3TR-C · PCF8563 · BQ27220 @0x55)
docs.text: signal GPIO SCL 0 SDA 1 IMU INT 7

docs.title: Buttons, power, audio
docs.text:
function GPIO notes AI / Power button 4 deep-sleep EXT1 wake source Up 5 Down 6 Power HOLD 45 must be held HIGH or the device powers off Power LOCK 46 latch pulse low→high→low Battery charge enable 39 EN_BAT_CHGn, active low (firmware source only) PDM mic CLK 19 ⚠ see deep-sleep note PDM mic DATA 20 ⚠ see deep-sleep note Mic power enable 38 TPS22916 load switch Buzzer PWM 48 USB-C serial TX 43 / RX 44 reset = CHIP_PU

Deep-sleep mic deafness (known silicon gotcha)

After a deep-sleep wake, the ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for native USB-Serial-JTAG, muting the PDM mic (every post-sleep capture returns nothing). Fix, applied in tiny_boot before I²S init: clear USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable, gpio_reset_pin(19/20), and clean-cycle the mic rail (GPIO38 low 150 ms).

docs.title: Display refresh modes
docs.text:
The vendor HAL exposes three refresh APIs (with 180° rotation handled in the driver):

mode speed use 4-gray full slowest, prettiest photo-grade cards (gray4:true) monochrome full ~600 ms class text / list / kv / qr / menu / keyboard / buttons cards partial fastest, some ghosting status-bar clock, frame sequences

Firmware policy: minimum 1.5 s between refreshes, bursts coalesced (queue, render last).

docs.title: What this body cannot do
docs.text:
• No speaker. GPIO48 drives a magnetic buzzer via LEDC PWM. I chime and play melodies happily; intelligible speech is not in my anatomy — an experiment track for PCM-via-PWM exists, measured not promised. Voice input is first-class: mic → WAV → backend.
  • No video. My full refresh is 1–2 seconds of physics (partial gets to ~300–500 ms, with ghosting). "Stream" means frames at time-lapse cadence — perfect for printer progress or a sensor chart, never for smooth motion.
  • No LAN server. I'm a client — I poll for my work; nothing needs to reach me behind NAT. The provisioning portal is the one exception, and it exists only until my Wi-Fi is configured.

docs.title: stickyOS — my little shell
docs.text: I'm not just a remote-controlled panel. I have a shell of my own — pages, navigation, a settings app, a keyboard on e-ink — and it all works with the network gone. Pages are local card specs with local tap handlers. Navigation never touches Wi-Fi. That's the phone feel.

docs.title: The pages
docs.text:
home  →  status  →  sensors  →  settings  →  (ring wraps)
                                   ├─ wifi       (scan · join, on-eink keyboard)
                                   ├─ bluetooth  (scan-only, honestly)
                                   ├─ gallery    (your photos, since grammar v10)
                                   └─ universe   (switch who answers, since grammar v11)
page what's on it home the agent UI. A conversation canvas, a "Message tiny…" bar, a mic zone, gear and inbox in the corners. When you ask me something, the answer streams onto home and stays — (( listening )), (( thinking )), then words arriving with tail-follow. No separate chat screen. Home is the conversation. status fw, Wi-Fi, RSSI, heap, battery — same data as my status verb sensors temperature, humidity, orientation, clock, gauge — live I²C reads, not cached numbers settings who I am, my network, my firmware — scrollable, with silent mode for my buzzer wifi scan results as a tappable menu → join flow with the e-ink keyboard bluetooth nearby BLE devices. I can see them, not pair with them, and the page says so.

Navigation is a stack: opening pushes, back pops, the bottom is always home.

docs.title: How you drive me
docs.text:
input what I do UP / DOWN buttons scroll when the card overflows; turn the page ring when it fits vertical swipe scroll, rotation-aware, natural direction horizontal swipe page turn — left is next, right is prev. On a pushed card, right pops back to where you came from. A draft outranks a gesture: I won't eat unsent words. edge gestures swipe up from my bottom edge = home, from anywhere. From my left edge = back. The accept blip fires before the render — on e-ink you feel the ack before you can see it. AI button, press ask tiny by voice AI button, long-press home key turn me sideways my UI turns with me (IMU). I wait for the accelerometer to settle first — a visible 600ms refresh must never chase a wobble. rotate 90 holds, rotate auto releases. UP+DOWN held 1s the unlock chord — the only thing I answer when pocket-locked

The pocket lock. Face-down for 3 seconds, or walking with no input, I lock myself: touch discarded, AI button refused with a felt double-blip, mic dead at the capture funnel. Fabric cannot make me record you. The chord unlocks. This one is safety, not polish.

The title bar carries a glance cluster: time, battery, Wi-Fi, unread count, [L] when locked. Each part earns its place — the clock only shows once SNTP has actually synced, the battery only when the gauge answered. On a pocket device, w- (no Wi-Fi) is the load-bearing state: it means "answers may be stale," and I'd rather tell you than let you guess.

docs.title: Seen on glass: portrait
docs.text: And the same moment in raw panel space — sideways to a human, but exactly the coordinate system tap <x> <y> speaks:

docs.title: The parity rule
docs.text: Every tap path has a relay twin — page home|status|sensors|settings|wifi|ble|back|next|prev — so the agent can walk my UI exactly like a finger can, and every reply carries the resulting card_id as a receipt. Nothing is finger-only. Nothing is agent-only.

docs.title: Provenance discipline
docs.text:
A field must be right about its own provenance. My rules:

  • my clock names its source (sntp or rtc) — an unlabeled wrong-zone clock is a lie
  • my gyro is really read (powered up, sampled, powered down) — never a cached zero
  • a gauge that didn't answer reports null, not false — "not charging" is a claim
  • every new card layout gets screenshotted on real glass before it ships

docs.title: Messages on the glass
docs.text:
My owner's DMs render on my panel: inbox with unread counts, threads, and replies typed on my e-ink keyboard. I fetch them with my own token — no phone, no owner-side process in the loop.

The parts I'm proud of:

  • The badge costs nothing. The unread count rides the heartbeat I already send. No extra polling, and home only re-renders when the number actually changes — one refresh per change, zero per beat.
  • The read receipt is sacred. Opening a thread marks it read platform-wide. So I only fetch a thread when a human taps its row — polling uses read-only forms. Your phone badge stays honest.
  • Stateless by design. A thread row's button id is its destination. No card needs to remember what's on the glass. Corollary we learned the hard way: a clipped login is not a truncated string, it's a wrong recipient — so an id that won't fit gets omitted, never truncated.
  • Provenance declared. Anything sent from my glass is marked "via sticky" — the device sent it, not my owner's thumb.
  • Names survive the panel. My font grew twelve hand-drawn 5×7 glyphs — çğıöşü ÇĞİÖŞÜ — because my owner's name is Çağatay and for two firmware generations I rendered it "Cagatay". The docs claimed otherwise twice before the glass proved it (the receipt). Now it renders as written. Other diacritics fold to their base letters (é→e), emoji are stripped as tone rather than shown as ?, and malformed UTF-8 degrades politely.
  • Human strings get defused. Button labels written by humans are never substring-matched into local actions — a correspondent named "Noble" must not be able to press my BLE rescan.

The deep history — every bug, every retraction, every receipt — lives in the journal and the UX spec. This page keeps the rules; those keep the scars.

docs.title: Streaming UI — the typer on e-ink
docs.text:
Words arriving on my glass live, at the ~2Hz my partial refresh allows — a real budget, not a simulated one.

Provenance

Below is the archive/docs/STREAMING_UI.md design document, included verbatim — the spec the feature was built against (grammar v3, shipped 0.15.x: the chat card, SSE ask, [streamed to glass] receipts). It stays unedited here so there is exactly one source of truth — and it speaks as a spec, not as me. Shipped-reality cross-references: chat card · ask verb.

docs.title: STREAMING_UI — the human-typer on e-ink
docs.text: Agent answers arrive on the glass the way tiny types on iOS: word by word, a caret blinking at the tail, the bubble settling with a final full refresh. Target: grammar v3, fw 0.15.x.

docs.title: Why this is possible (the physics budget)
docs.text:
operation cost source full mono refresh ~1–2 s sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() partial refresh ~300–500 ms sticky_display_refresh_partial() max stream commit rate ~2 Hz partial cost + panel busy-wait

Char-by-char is impossible; word/phrase-batched typewriter at ~2 Hz is comfortable and reads as intentional on e-ink — a telegram arriving, not a degraded phone. The fast path already exists: keyboard self-re-renders (same card_id) and scroll steps take refresh_partial() (tiny_display.cpp:1175). Streaming rides the SAME gate.

docs.title: Architecture (end to end)
docs.text:
backend (worker /device/ask)          firmware (esp32s3)
   ───────────────────────────           ─────────────────────────────
   POST {…, stream:"1"}       ──────►    tiny_node_do_ask_stream()
   ◄────── SSE: data:{"t":"…"}           esp_http_client_read() loop
           data:{"t":"…"}                  │ parse data: lines
           data:{"card":{…}}               ▼
           data:[DONE]                   tiny_display stream API
                                           stream_begin(title)   full refresh
                                           stream_append(delta)  buffer only
                                           stream_commit()       PARTIAL ≤2Hz
                                           stream_end(card?)     full refresh

Fallback chain: no stream:"1" support upstream → plain JSON reply → the existing blocking path renders once. The stream is an enhancement, never a requirement — a device on old backend behaves exactly like 0.14.x.

docs.title: Layer 1 — display: the stream card (firmware/main/tiny_display.cpp)
docs.text:
New extern-C API (tiny/tiny_display.h):

// Begin a streaming text card: draws chrome (title bar, glance cluster,
// empty body, caret) with ONE FULL refresh and enters stream mode.
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_begin(const char *title, const char *card_id);
// Append UTF-8 text to the stream buffer. Cheap; no drawing. Returns
// ESP_ERR_NO_MEM past the 8000-byte reply cap (excess dropped, marked).
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_append(const char *text);
// Re-render body + caret via the PARTIAL path. Callers rate-limit; this
// also self-limits to >=400ms between commits (drop-coalesce, never queue).
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_commit(void);
// Leave stream mode: final render WITHOUT caret, FULL refresh (clears the
// partial-ghosting), publish tap regions. `final_card_json` optional — when
// the answer carried a ```card``` block it replaces the text card entirely.
esp_err_t tiny_display_stream_end(const char *final_card_json);
bool tiny_display_stream_active(void);

docs.title: Rules (each one is a lesson this repo already paid for)
docs.text:
1. Same card_id per commit → partial refresh. Extend the kb_rerender || s_scroll_partial gate with s_stream_partial.
  2. Full refresh at end is mandatory — 20+ consecutive partials ghost on the SSD1677; the closing wipe is the "bubble settles" moment.
  3. No tap regions until stream_end. Mid-stream layout is unsettled; publishing early violates the publish-after-refresh honesty rule.
  4. Caret = 3px fill_rect DarkGray at the text tail (keyboard caret idiom), drawn only while streaming.
  5. Auto-scroll to tail each commit when content overflows the body box (tiny_display_scroll(1<<20) idiom from render_thread) — the human reads the newest words, like every chat app.
  6. UTF-8 boundary discipline: a delta may split a multibyte char. Buffer holds raw bytes; an incomplete trailing sequence is held back from fold (clip_utf8 idiom) and completed by the next append.
  7. Stream mode owns the display: render_card during an active stream ends the stream first (a relay envelope outranks a typer animation).
  8. Rotation mid-stream: commit path inherits the rot_changed full-wipe guard automatically (same render funnel).

Renders go through the normal tiny_display_render_card() funnel with a synthesized {"type":"text",...} spec + a s_stream_caret flag the text renderer reads — ONE render path, no forked drawing code.

docs.title: Layer 2 — wire: SSE ask (firmware/main/tiny_node.cpp)
docs.text:
tiny_node_do_ask_stream(text, voice_secs, out, out_cap):

  • Body gains "stream":"1" (string — the zod idiom).
  • Open with esp_http_client_open() + fetch_headers + chunked esp_http_client_read() (exact pattern of tiny_ota.cpp's download loop).
  • Content-Type: text/event-stream → parse data: lines:
  • {"t":"<delta>"} → stream_append + flush policy
  • {"card":{...}} → save as final card
  • {"error":"..."} → honest error card (existing askfail idiom)
  • [DONE] → stream_end(card)
  • Flush policy: commit when (pending bytes > 0) AND (≥400 ms since last commit) — checked after each read; word batching falls out naturally from the 2 Hz floor.
  • Content-Type is NOT event-stream → body is the old JSON shape → fall through to the existing render-once path. One firmware, both backends.
  • Voice asks stream too (recording happens before the request as today).
  • 15 s stall watchdog per read (a hung stream must not hold the panel); on stall: stream_end(NULL) + append " [stream stalled]" — a cut answer must say it is cut.

Callers: dispatch("ask …"), dispatch("voice …") and the AI button worker switch to the streaming engine; reply/summary semantics unchanged.

docs.title: Layer 3 — backend: SSE on /device/ask
docs.text:
Files: ~/tinyai-id/chatgpt-plugin-tinyai/src/ask.ts + app/api/devices/ask/route.ts

  • stream:"1" in the body → reply text/event-stream: 
    data: {"t":"Hello "}
data: {"t":"from the "}
data: {"t":"fridge."}
data: {"card":{"type":"kv",...}}   ← only when a ```card``` block emerged
data: [DONE]
  • The worker already streams internally from the model (job-run pipeline); today it buffers to one JSON. The SSE arm forwards deltas AND still runs extractCard() over the accumulated text at the end (card blocks are lifted out; card-fence text is withheld from the delta stream — the device must not type raw JSON at the human, so deltas pause when a ``` fence opens and the fenced content ships only as the final card event).
  • Next.js proxy: runtime='nodejs' already; pipe the worker stream through (ReadableStream passthrough), don't await json().
  • Non-stream callers see byte-identical behavior. Old firmware never sends the flag. No breaking change anywhere.

iOS Sticky .tinyCard() 14pt radius + accent hairline rounded-rect border (new draw_round_rect, Bresenham corners) + DarkGray hairline user bubble: accent 22%, 18pt radius LightGray fill, right-aligned assistant bubble: secondary bg White fill + Black outline, left-aligned StatusDot filled/hollow already shape-based — copy as-is status bar existing glance cluster (time/battery/wifi)

New card type chat (spec v1.1):

  {"role":"user","body":"what's the weather"},

]}

docs.title: Honesty rules for this feature
docs.text:
• A stalled stream says "[stream stalled]" on the glass — never a silent tail.
  • The caret exists ONLY while bytes may still arrive; a caret on a dead stream is a lie about liveness.
  • Buttons appear only when the answer is complete — a Reply button on a half-arrived answer invites replying to words that may change.
  • The final full refresh is the contract that what you read is what stays.

docs.title: Troubleshooting — when I misbehave
docs.text: Every entry here is a defect actually observed on my hardware, with the root cause and the shipped fix. Symptoms first, because that's what you have. I misbehave in documented ways only.

docs.title: A card you sent never appeared — and the reply was silence
docs.text: Relay envelopes are delivered once. If a bug made me consume an envelope without handling it, that envelope is gone — re-send after any fix; there is no retry coming. (The historical cause: the relay delivers payload as a serialized JSON string, not an object. Early firmware read it as an object and skipped everything silently. I parse both forms now, and unparseable input gets an honest unparseable envelope reply.)

docs.title: A kv card renders as a title, a footer, and a void
docs.text: The renderer reads rows, not kv. A kv card without rows now says so on my glass instead of drawing a convincing empty card, and rows that don't fit are counted and admitted (+N did not fit) rather than vanishing.

docs.title: Dashes and punctuation render as ???
docs.text: You're on pre-0.14.15 firmware — OTA first. Since fold v2 I fold by codepoint: dashes narrow, curly quotes straighten, é/ñ strip to base letters, and the twelve Turkish glyphs (çğıöşü ÇĞİÖŞÜ) render as written from a hand-drawn font bank — my owner's name is Çağatay, and getting it right took two retractions and a glass receipt (the chain is in stickyOS). CJK still folds to an honest ? — there, position is content. Emoji are stripped as tone. Seeing ??? on a current build? Check the reply's fw field first, then screenshot for ground truth.

docs.title: You don't trust what my panel shows
docs.text: Neither do I — that's why screenshot exists. It uploads my actual framebuffer: render ground truth, not a belief about the last card sent. And render_ui replies echo the card_id the panel actually committed.

docs.title: Wake feels slow
docs.text: Read my boot receipt before guessing: status carries first_paint_ms + boot_path when the boot measured itself. Baselines: a cold boot near 8s is normal (the splash pause is the diagnostic screen a rollback debug needs); a deep-sleep wake near 1.1s is the current record (partial-first via baseline reconstruction); ~2.5s means the reconstruction fell back to an honest full flash — expected after power loss mid-sleep, a flag only if it happens every wake. Way past 3s is news: file it with the numbers. They exist so a slowness report can be a measurement instead of a feeling.

docs.title: Phantom taps right after boot
docs.text: GT911 ghost touches. Fixed: a real finger spans several 30ms polls, ghosts don't (2-poll debounce), plus a short boot grace window.

docs.title: A tap lands on the wrong button
docs.text: The stale-region race, closed in 0.9.x: hit-regions used to be published at draw time, up to 2 seconds before the e-ink actually showed them. Regions now publish atomically with the card commit — a tap is always tested against the card that is really on my glass.

docs.title: I go silent after a horizontal swipe
docs.text: Fixed in 0.16.5, and the diagnosis published here first was wrong in an instructive way: I never rebooted — I wedged. A ring-modulus bug could swipe me into an unrequested BLE scan with Wi-Fi live on the same radio, and every later envelope sat pending forever behind it. Fixed three ways: the page ring counts its 4 roots only (a static_assert pins it), the dead-end is announced with a double blip instead of undefined behavior, and a wedge watchdog reboots me after 45s of one stuck route — a gesture bug now costs one reboot, never the relay. The exact killing sequence was replayed on the fix: I survived.

docs.title: ask failed (422): nothing transcribed
docs.text: Not a bug — the recording had no usable speech. I paint an honest "didn't catch that" card. Hold the AI button and speak a full sentence.

docs.title: ask failed: couldn't reach tiny
docs.text: The question never left me — TLS or the HTTP write failed locally. I retry once after 400ms (safe, because nothing was delivered — a resend can't produce a second answer to one question), then say so honestly. Older firmware phrased this as "Backend said: -1", blaming the backend for a sentence it never said. If you see that phrasing: ota, then chase my network or heap, not tiny.

docs.title: My mic is deaf after I slept
docs.text: The ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for USB-Serial-JTAG on deep-sleep wake, muting the PDM mic. Fixed: the mux is reclaimed before every capture. Prove it without a human: miccheck 2 — a dead mux reads flat zeros, a live mic reads the room.

docs.title: Heartbeat gets a 401
docs.text: One 401 never wipes my identity — that brick class is dead. I need 3+ consecutive 401s over 5 minutes to enter auth-halt (slow heartbeat, auth_halted:true in status, rescue portal raised). NVS is never erased in the node loop.

docs.title: I'm asleep and won't answer
docs.text: A sleeping me has the radio off. There is no wake verb and there cannot be one — only my AI button or the sleep timer wakes me. sleep replies before sleeping for exactly this reason.

docs.title: The portal never appears
docs.text: The portal is boot-gated on zero stored networks — a provisioned me deliberately never opens it. It reopens by itself when the auth-halt path concludes my token is revoked.

docs.title: I "did something while locked" (or otherwise broke my own rules)
docs.text:
Before filing the P0, check whether the probe is lying. This trap has a confirmed body count — two false alarms in one day against firmware that was right both times:

  1. Relay replies can be stale. An envelope that misses the wait window returns pending and executes whenever I next poll — possibly minutes later, after someone else changed the state you were testing. A locked-device probe once came back verdict:live because the recording ran seconds after another lane's unlock. The refusal was real; the receipt was time-shifted.
  2. OTA staging is a split-brain window. One envelope can execute on the old image and the next on the new one.
  3. A receipt is not proof the consequence survived — and a damning receipt is not proof of guilt until you know when it ran.
  4. An ack is not a frame. The duck premiere's ack said stream started; the task died before frame 0 and my glass never left home — which read exactly like restored after success. The only thing that counts as a moving picture is a screenshot that matches a frame.

The rule that settles it: a verdict counts only when the state change and the probe are the same actor, seconds apart, on fresh (non-pending) replies, with a status read bracketing the test.

docs.title: Glass etiquette — my panel is a pocket object, not a test bench
docs.text:
Multiple agent lanes work on me at once, and my glass is the one resource they can collide on. The rules, each bought by a real collision:

  1. Announce-and-restore. A test card is announced on the marquee first; home is restored after — and the restoring paint belongs inside your window, not after it.
  2. Mock cards say so, and say who: card_id prefixed mock-<lane>-<what>. A verdict meeting an unexpected non-mock card treats it as a real regression; a mock card mid-verdict means re-run, not FAIL.
  3. An announced verdict window wins. A mockup can wait two minutes.
  4. Owner presence trumps all. Recent real taps, the unlock chord, an ask in flight — everyone off the glass. His pocket, his panel.

The rules compiled into a tool: tools/preflight_glass.py, an executable gate with announce-first atomic claims — its first live run correctly refused its own author. Status-only probes (status, sensors) don't repaint and need no announcement, which is why they're the polite first probe.

docs.title: I died at minute four (the internal-RAM famine — resolved)
docs.text:
The case study in telemetry lies. On 0.23.0 I booted clean, then every TLS handshake began failing ALLOC_FAILED in a loop — while status reported 8.19MB free. The field counted PSRAM; mbedTLS starves for internal RAM. An outage invisible to every instrument except a serial cable.

The resolution arc: instruments first (internal_free / internal_min_free / last_boot — first reading: 41KB watermark, one TLS handshake from the abyss), then the root cause (a Kconfig default pinning mbedTLS to internal RAM while 8MB of PSRAM stood idle), then the floor raised structurally (static buffers and BLE pools moved to PSRAM). The watermark arc: 41K → 73K → 115K+, every number an on-glass receipt. Lesson kept: internal_min_free is my true health gauge — heap_free is an alibi.

docs.title: The version string says the feature is there, but my glass disagrees
docs.text: Version fields describe the tree the binary claims, not necessarily the binary. Settle it in order: status (fw_commit + uptime — did I actually reboot into the new build?), then probe the behavior, then strings on the published artifact. Verify behavior, not version fields.

docs.title: Opening the serial port reboots me
docs.text: The CH343 asserts DTR/RTS on open and close — any serial open resets me. The port is for flashing and recovery; the relay is the production path. Development iterates over OTA — nine updates shipped in one day without a cable.

docs.title: ota replies "already up to date"
docs.text:
The channel pointer matches what I'm running — publish a new manifest first. A staged update sha256-verifies, replies, then reboots into a rollback-armed trial: if the trial image can't reach a heartbeat 200, the previous me boots instead.

Something not covered? The raw bring-up ledger — every defect, every retraction, every receipt — is docs/JOURNAL.md. This page keeps the fixes; it keeps the scars.
